name: Ezra Booth
role: Methodist minister who joined, then publicly opposed the Church
dateNote: Section 52 sent him to Missouri in June 1831; he was barred from preaching on 6 September 1831.
importance: Ezra Booth was a Methodist minister from Mantua, Ohio, who joined in 1831. Section 52 sends him to Missouri with Isaac Morley, but he was barred from preaching soon after his return. Section 64 says the Lord was angry with him and Morley for not keeping the law. From September 1831 he published nine letters against the Church, which prompted section 71.
connections: His companion was Isaac Morley; Sidney Rigdon later challenged his published claims.

sources.title: Ezra Booth, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Birth (14 Feb. 1792), ordination, silencing and letters checked on JSP. JSP gives only a burial date of 12 Jan. 1873, so the death is given as about 1873. The link to section 71 comes from that study file.
